definitions: A vessel of vast tonnage engineered to ferry several thousand passengers across open water while never once appearing to hurry.
colloq. The kind of ship that treats a harbor skyline as competition and a buffet line as a load-bearing structure.
example: The tugboats fussed over the thiccc cruise ship for twenty minutes before it deigned to notice the dock.
etymology: From cruise (Dutch 'kruisen,' to cross or sail to and fro) plus ship (Old English 'scip'). Liner descends from the shipping lines such vessels once ran on fixed schedule, back when punctuality outranked the pool deck.
caption: Plate N., A cruise ship of considerable draft, treating the harbor as a parking suggestion.
